headline: Exploited Zero-Days, AI Hacking, and Healthcare Cyberattacks Dominate News
summary:
**Critical Vulnerabilities Under Active Exploitation**:

*   **[UPDATE] Citrix Zero-Days and Oracle PeopleSoft Flaw Under Active Exploit**: New research reveals CVE-2026-35273 is a chain of three vulnerabilities in Oracle PeopleSoft, enabling unauthenticated RCE. A critical workaround involves editing the `allowedhosts.properties` file.
*   **[UPDATE] PHP2Shell: Critical Flaws Trigger Emergency Patches, Mass Scans**: A China-linked APT group is exploiting PHP2Shell in conjunction with a Linux kernel flaw to gain root access on firewalls, compromising at least 25 devices, including a U.S. government-affiliated organization.
*   **[NEW] CISA Adds Exploited Google Brotli and Adobe Commerce Flaws to KEV**: CISA has added two actively exploited vulnerabilities, Node2Shell (CVE-2026-111497) in Google Brotli and a file upload flaw in Adobe Commerce/Magento (CVE-2026-48356), to its KEV catalog, mandating patching for federal agencies.

**Emerging Threats and Industry Responses**:

*   **[NEW] AI-Powered Hacking Tools Like CyberStrikeAI Used in Japan Attacks**: Three cyberattack campaigns targeting Japanese organizations demonstrate the increasing use of AI in offensive operations, with one campaign leveraging CyberStrikeAI to automate the attack lifecycle.
*   **[NEW] GMO Internet Group Offers $1M Bounty After Refusing Ransom Demand**: Following a breach of its 'Onamae.com Desktop Cloud' service, GMO Internet Group has launched a $1 million bounty program to identify attackers after refusing a $50 million ransom demand.

**Healthcare Sector Under Pressure**:

*   **[NEW] UNM Health Services Disrupted by Cyberattack, Extortion Group Claims Data Theft**: The University of New Mexico Health system experienced a significant cyberattack causing major disruptions, with an extortion group claiming responsibility for data theft.

**Policy and Investment News**:

*   **[NEW] White House Launches 'Project Lifeline 250' to Secure Rural Hospitals**: The White House has initiated a six-month pilot program to enhance the cybersecurity of underserved rural hospitals through public-private partnerships.
*   **[NEW] AI Security Startup Upwind Raises $400M, Valuation Soars to $3.8B**: Upwind Security, an AI application security startup, has secured $400 million in Series C funding, reflecting strong investor interest in cloud and AI security solutions.

articles.headline: Citrix Zero-Days and Oracle PeopleSoft Flaw Under Active Exploit
articles.title: Threat Advisory: Citrix & Oracle Flaws Actively Exploited
articles.excerpt: A critical threat alert has been issued for two Citrix NetScaler zero-day vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-88771, CVE-2026-88772) and a re-weaponized Oracle PeopleSoft flaw (CVE-2026-35273). All three vulnerabilities are being actively exploited in the wild for remote code execution. CISA has added the Citrix flaws to its KEV catalog, and the ShinyHunters group is reportedly using new techniques to exploit the Oracle vulnerability, targeting multiple sectors beyond higher education.
articles.updateSummary: Oracle PeopleSoft flaw CVE-2026-35273 revealed as a 3-bug chain involving SSRF and default trust misconfiguration.
articles.updateContent: New research from the Zero Day Initiative details that CVE-2026-35273 is not a single flaw but a complex chain of three vulnerabilities. It combines a Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) in the Integration Gateway, a default trust misconfiguration in the Management Hub (PSEMHUB) allowing local loopback trust, and a third bug for arbitrary code execution. This chain enables unauthenticated RCE. Affected versions include PeopleTools 8.61 and 8.62. A critical workaround involves editing the `allowedhosts.properties` file to remove `127.0.0.1` and `localhost` entries, breaking the trust relationship exploited by the chain.

articles.headline: PHP2Shell: Critical Flaws Trigger Emergency Patches, Mass Scans
articles.title: PHP2Shell Flaws Spark Emergency Patches and Mass Exploitation
articles.excerpt: Two critical remote code execution vulnerabilities in PHP, dubbed 'PHP2Shell' and tracked as CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, have led to widespread scanning and exploitation. The flaws affect the core PHP interpreter, allowing unauthenticated attackers to execute code on vulnerable web servers. Emergency patches have been released, but pre-disclosure exploitation was observed, highlighting the significant risk to millions of websites using platforms like WordPress, Drupal, and Magento. CISA has issued an urgent alert, as the bugs can lead to server compromise, data theft, or denial of service.
articles.updateSummary: China-linked APT exploits PHP2Shell and Fragnesia to root firewalls, targeting U.S. government entities.
articles.updateContent: A China-linked APT group is actively exploiting PHP2Shell (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619) in combination with a Linux kernel privilege escalation flaw, Fragnesia (CVE-2026-46300), to gain root access on internet-facing firewalls. The campaign involves reconnaissance using FOFA, leading to the compromise of 25 firewalls, including one belonging to a U.S. government-affiliated organization. Attackers deploy PHP webshells and establish reverse SSH tunnels for persistence, indicating a highly targeted and sophisticated operation with espionage motives. This represents a significant escalation in the threat landscape for PHP2Shell.

articles.headline: UNM Health Services Disrupted by Cyberattack, Extortion Group Claims Data Theft
articles.title: UNM Health Cyberattack Disrupts Patient Care
articles.excerpt: The University of New Mexico (UNM) Health system experienced a significant cyberattack on October 26, 2026, causing major disruptions to clinical operations, including the diversion of ambulances and cancellation of surgeries. A new extortion group calling itself "BYOD" has claimed responsibility, alleging the theft of a massive trove of sensitive patient, student, and employee data. While UNM Health has since restored critical systems, the incident highlights the severe operational risks facing the healthcare sector.

articles.headline: CISA Adds Exploited Google Brotli and Adobe Commerce Flaws to KEV
articles.title: CISA Adds Brotli & Adobe Flaws to KEV Catalog
articles.excerpt: The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) has added two actively exploited vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog. The flaws include a critical out-of-bounds write in Google's Brotli library, dubbed Node2Shell (CVE-2026-111497), and a file upload vulnerability in Adobe Commerce/Magento (CVE-2026-48356). Federal agencies are now mandated to patch by November 10, 2026.

articles.headline: AI-Powered Hacking Tools Like CyberStrikeAI Used in Japan Attacks
articles.title: AI Hacking Tools Target Japanese Organizations
articles.excerpt: Security researchers have uncovered three distinct cyberattack campaigns targeting Japanese organizations that demonstrate the increasing operational use of artificial intelligence in offensive operations. One notable campaign leveraged an open-source AI penetration testing framework named CyberStrikeAI, which used a swarm of 44 AI agents to automate the entire attack lifecycle, from reconnaissance to data exfiltration, against at least 19 organizations.

articles.headline: GMO Internet Group Offers $1M Bounty After Refusing Ransom Demand
articles.title: GMO Offers $1M Bounty to Catch Hackers
articles.excerpt: Following a breach of its 'Onamae.com Desktop Cloud' service, Japanese tech giant GMO Internet Group has refused to pay a ransom demand of approximately $50 million. Instead, the company has launched a $1 million 'GMO Cybercrime Bounty' program to identify and lead to the arrest of the attackers. GMO is also offering compensation to affected customers and has actively worked to take down the hackers' data leak site.

articles.headline: White House Launches 'Project Lifeline 250' to Secure Rural Hospitals
articles.title: White House Launches Rural Hospital Cyber Pilot
articles.excerpt: The White House, through the Office of the National Cyber Director (ONCD), has launched 'Project Lifeline 250,' a six-month pilot program designed to bolster the cybersecurity of underserved rural hospitals. Kicking off in South Carolina, the initiative is a public-private partnership providing free cybersecurity hardware, services, and support from technology companies like Microsoft, Cisco, and Zscaler to facilities that often lack the resources to defend against modern cyber threats.

articles.headline: AI Security Startup Upwind Raises $400M, Valuation Soars to $3.8B
articles.title: Upwind Security Raises $400M at $3.8B Valuation
articles.excerpt: Upwind Security, a startup specializing in cloud and AI application security, has closed a $400 million Series C funding round, pushing its valuation to $3.8 billion. The round, led by Bessemer Venture Partners, reflects surging investor interest and confidence in platforms designed to secure complex cloud environments and the rapidly growing deployment of AI models and agents.
